truth: only a component write needs a target check (retro kit-p1-security-guards Δ6). A call that cannot be
a BComponent write is no write: a one-argument set(v) (AtomicReference, ThreadLocal), a numeric literal first
argument (JDBC setInt(1, v), List.set(0, x)), and a receiver declared in the file as a PreparedStatement, a
List, an Atomic*, a Calendar or a ThreadLocal; a file with only those is no "servlet writes" either (no
no-csrf row). A.java carries each of them by receiver type, C.java by the call alone (receivers of no declared type). B.java carries the writes that stay rows: a component write
(target.set(p, v, op), setDouble), a receiver of an unknown type, a receiver declared both as a List and as a
BComponent, a call that spans lines (its argument count is unknown), a plain write on the same line as a
component write, and invoke(...).
